solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

parts.note: a stub is the short remnant left of a pencil or cigarette

indicators.note: said tells us a word is spoken, so we write what it sounds like

parts.note: a bourn is a small stream, chiefly in southern England

explanation.surface: A stubborn bit of debris sits beside a brook that someone mentions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' makes BOURN, the stream, come out as BORN, its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inflexible refuses to budge, which is exactly what an obstinate person does.

indicators.note: redeveloped suggests a site rebuilt in new form, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Certain locations, that is, have been rebuilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redeveloped' rearranges PLACESIE, the letters of 'places ie', into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Especial is a formal synonym for particular or special, as in 'of especial importance'.

clue.text: Easily approachable female in a story

indicators.note: in places the female abbreviation inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: a fable is a short moral story

explanation.surface: A friendly woman appears as a character in a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts F inside A FABLE, straight after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone affable is friendly and pleasant, so others find them easy to approach.

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Unlike landlubbers, a few seamen hurl abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes part of 'Whereas sailors': wherASSAILors.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail can mean to criticise someone fiercely in words, not just to attack physically.

clue.text: Kay with one young lady at island capital

parts.note: Kay is how the letter K is spelt out
the Roman numeral I is one
gal is an informal word for a girl or young woman
I is a common abbreviation for island on maps

explanation.surface: Kay and a girl travel together to the capital of an island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: KIGALI is the capital of Rwanda, which is landlocked, so 'island capital' misleads: island only gives the final I.
explanation.definitionFit: Kigali is the capital city of Rwanda in central Africa.

clue.text: Remove half a stone, it's the trend

indicators.note: read as re-move, to move again, so the letters of the following words are shifted into a new order

parts.note: the contraction gives its three letters, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Losing seven pounds is all the rage right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remove' rearranges HALFASTONEITS, the letters of 'half a stone it's'. The surface tempts you to take away part of a word; nothing is deleted.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest fashion is whatever is currently in vogue, which is what a trend is.

parts.note: read literally, a woman who is waiting patiently; in fact the title of a noblewoman serving a queen or princess

explanation.surface: A long-suffering woman who serves someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading: a lady who is waiting, and so patient.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady-in-waiting is a noblewoman who attends a queen or princess at court.

parts.note: the British and Irish Lions rugby team stir patriotism, but a group of lions is called a pride, so lions belonging to a nation form one

explanation.surface: The patriotic glow when the Lions rugby side plays.
explanation.walkthrough: The British and Irish Lions are a touring rugby union team; a group of lions is a 'pride', which gives the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: National pride is the patriotic feeling of being proud of one's country.

parts.note: consumer looks like a shopper, but here it is someone who literally consumes, that is eats

explanation.surface: Something a shopper might care about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumer' suggests retail; read it as an eater, and what interests an eater is what can be eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fit to be eaten is what matters to someone who consumes food.

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary, so the letters before it are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: Martha owns a remarkable flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' rearranges MARTHAAN. A 'bloomer' is a mistake or knickers, but here it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaranth is a plant with showy tassels of flowers, so a thing that blooms.

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A dense dark loaf of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a description of the loaf; it is a business, CO.
explanation.definitionFit: A cob is a round, crusty loaf of bread in British baking.

clue.text: Viol, it played in town near Rome

indicators.note: played suggests the viol being performed on, and signals its letters being rearranged with the next word's

explanation.surface: A viol was performed in a small Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges VIOLIT. The viol is an old stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Tivoli is a hill town east of Rome, famous for the Villa d'Este gardens.

parts.note: sounds like a darling being beaten, but describes a sweet on a stick that is licked

explanation.surface: A beloved child gets a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetie' looks like a term of endearment and 'licking' a beating; read them as a confection and literal licking.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a hard sweet on a stick, eaten by licking it.

indicators.note: Cleopatra holds two men's names, the run at its start and PAT later, and first picks the earlier one
in tells us the run lies inside the word that follows
the word's outer letters embrace the run, holding it within them

explanation.surface: The earliest lover held in the Egyptian queen's arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First', 'in' and 'embrace' locate the run at the start of 'Cleopatra's': cLEOpatra.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is a common male first name, so stands for a man in crossword usage.

clue.text: Cheat to be successful in damaged sled

indicators.note: in places the winning word inside the rearranged letters
damaged means broken up, so the letters of the sled are rearranged

parts.note: to win is to be successful

explanation.surface: A racer cheats to win though their sledge is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges the sled's letters and 'in' sets the winning piece inside them; picture a damaged sledge, but nothing is literally broken.
explanation.definitionFit: To swindle is to cheat someone, especially out of money.

parts.note: D is the fourth grade after A, B and C, so fourth-rate
Ry is the abbreviation for railway, which runs on lines

explanation.surface: Poor-quality lines of verse are dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' suggests poetry; it is railway lines, RY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry speech or book is dull and lacks interest.

indicators.note: desperate suggests wild and frantic, so the letters of the name are thrown about

explanation.surface: Antoine is a student in despair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperate' rearranges ANTOINE. Eton is an English boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: An Etonian is a pupil, or former pupil, of Eton College.

clue.text: Try some luggage that could create a precedent

parts.note: to test is to try something out
a case is a suitcase, one piece of luggage

explanation.surface: An experiment with a suitcase that might set a legal example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'luggage' points to travel; the answer is a lawsuit whose verdict others will follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A test case is a lawsuit whose outcome sets a precedent for later similar cases.

indicators.note: coming from says the letters are produced out of the word, reshaped into something new

parts.note: in Roman numerals 99 is IC, one before a hundred

explanation.surface: A narcotic found in a carton of ninety-nine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming from' rearranges the carton's letters. Writing 99 as IC is a crossword licence: strict Roman numerals give XCIX.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic is a drug that dulls the senses, such as opium.

definitions.meaning: taking a hard line with no middle ground
furthest out, as in the ... edge of a region

explanation.definitionFit: Extreme means both holding radical views and situated at the very farthest point.

clue.text: Jack's bag is a song with punch

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song
to box is to punch

explanation.surface: A sailor's bag is described as a tune with a hit in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack, or Jack tar, is a sailor; a ditty box held his small belongings.
explanation.definitionFit: A ditty box is a small container in which a sailor kept sewing gear and personal items.

indicators.note: sound here means said aloud, so we write the spelling that matches the spoken word

parts.note: a toxin is a poison

explanation.surface: Someone is poisoned, so raise the alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound the alarm' reads as one phrase; 'sound' is the indicator and 'alarm' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is an alarm bell or warning signal.

indicators.note: not says the following word's letters are left out of the report

parts.note: a bulletin is a short news report

explanation.surface: A shell is missing from the account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not in' tempts as one phrase; 'not' removes IN from BULLETIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullet is a projectile fired from a gun, loosely called a shell.

indicators.note: in places the trip inside the postal district letters

parts.note: SE is the south-east London postal district
a trip is a tour or journey

explanation.surface: A music group tours in a part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians; it is a strip of colour. SE is the postcode area for south-east London.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a long narrow band of colour on a surface.

clue.text: Teetotaller's round included quantity of spirits

indicators.note: included says the round letter is put inside the abstainer's letters

parts.note: TT is the abbreviation for teetotal or a teetotaller; the run of the answer inside this word is a coincidence
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A non-drinker's round still featured a dram of whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teetotaller's round' looks like a round of drinks; it gives TT and O separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small measure of spirits such as rum or whisky.

definitions.meaning: shaped like a globe, so round
a leaflet sent round to many people

explanation.definitionFit: Circular means round in shape and also names a printed notice distributed widely.

parts.note: a chef is a cook
the Roman numeral I is one
E for east, the oriental direction

explanation.surface: The chef had one Asian biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oriental' looks like a description of the biscuit; it gives E for east.
explanation.definitionFit: Cookie is the American word for a biscuit, now common in Britain too.

parts.note: pictures a rocket steered by a navigation gadget, which is how a self-steering weapon works

explanation.surface: A rocket fitted with a satellite navigation device.
explanation.walkthrough: Satnav, satellite navigation, guides a car; a rocket so steered is a weapon directed to its target.
explanation.definitionFit: A guided missile is a rocket-propelled weapon steered to its target in flight.
